Since its creation, the Hub has worked with 160 WHO member states, 190 partner organisations and thousands of scientists and policymakers to strengthen global disease surveillance. The plan focuses on five key initiatives, including using artificial intelligence to identify potential health threats, strengthening genomic sequencing to track emerging pathogens and connecting experts in data science and disease modelling. It will also support countries in sharing health data securely and improving cooperation between human, animal and environmental health systems.

Konneh has asked the United States to impose Global Magnitsky sanctions on people who enable mining licensing deals in Liberia and move the proceeds into US real estate, telling a Washington policy audience that the country faces its gravest threat since the civil war and the Ebola epidemic. Konneh made the request Oct. 7 at a private roundtable convened by the National Endowment for Democracy in Washington, according to a statement his office released Oct. 12. He also asked Washington to support court monitoring in Liberia, resume mentoring of law enforcement officers vetted by the US Drug Enforcement Administration "with appropriate oversight," and engage the Treasury Department's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network on active financial intelligence cases. "Liberia is not yet a captured state. But we are at the most dangerous point since the civil war and the Ebola epidemic," Konneh said. "My request is straightforward: help us establish transparent regulations before agreements are finalized, and support impartial enforcement of the law after confiscation, whether the suspect is an airport baggage handler, a police crimes director, a former Vice President, or a multinational corporation." The platform is an initiative of the CJID developed in partnership with the US-based research nonprofit Media Ecosystem Analysis Group (MEAG) to strengthen access to structured and verifiable public health information across the continent. At a time when access to reliable, contextual, and timely information about public health policies and commitments is increasingly important, SautiHealth makes a significant contribution to strengthening transparency, media reporting, and research across Africa. The platform automatically collects and organises public statements from verified sources, including media reports, press releases, institutional websites, interviews, and public broadcasts. By centralising this fragmented information, SautiHealth will help journalists, researchers, and civil society actors identify trends, compare statements over time, and better understand how health narratives evolve across countries and institutions.

Photograph: Ollie Hammick Review Gabrielle Goliath: Elegy review – devastating lament is a furious, single-note call to action Ibraaz, London Too controversial for the Venice Biennale, this haunting video and audio work commemorates murders and genocides with an angry act of mourning T he sound of mourning spills out into the streets. A single, endless wailing note echoes out of the basement of Ibraaz, a relatively new cultural centre in London’s Fitzrovia. This is Gabrielle Goliath’s heart-wrenching Elegy, each of its three films featuring a woman singing just one note until their lungs falter and another woman steps up to fill in for her.

Une fuite précipitée par la mutinerie des militaires du Capsat, faisant suite au soulèvement de la Gen Z. Un an après ces événements, RFI s'intéresse ce matin à la diplomatie menée par le chef de la transition, Michaël Randrianirina. Celui-ci défend une « diplomatie tous azimuts », selon ses propres mots. En un an, la Grande Île s'est fortement rapprochée de la Russie tout en maintenant des relations soutenues avec ses partenaires occidentaux.

Intitulée « Une répression brutale bafoue les droits des personnes LGBT », l'enquête menée par l'ONG internationale s'appuie sur 39 témoignages pour dénoncer la dégradation des conditions de vie des citoyens sénégalais homosexuels et trans depuis le vote de la loi qui renforce la répression à leur encontre via la modification de l’article 319 du code pénal. stories.title: Mourners killed by Kenya police at Odinga national farewell not part of violence, BBC finds
stories.summary: Figure caption, "There were so many people, why him?" Yvonne Akinyi remembers the day her husband was shot dead Published 12 October 2026 Three mourners killed when Kenyan police opened fire at a national farewell for former Prime Minister Raila Odinga were not involved in a clash that sparked gunfire, a BBC Africa Eye investigation has found. During an event held last October for people to pay their respects to Odinga, three people were shot dead after mourners attempted to gain access to the VIP section of Nairobi's Kasarani Stadium by force. BBC analysis from inside the stadium shows the victims were each between at least 60m (197 ft) and 160m from the scuffles. Kenya's Interior Minister Kipchumba Murkomen told the BBC that the police action had been "restrained" after the crowd starting throwing stones. In footage analysed by the BBC, it is clear that objects, including plastic chairs, are thrown, but we have no evidence that they included stones.

stories.title: Dozens of gold prospectors killed in strikes on Egypt-Sudan border, rights group says
stories.summary: Image source, Getty Images Image caption, File photo of gold prospectors in northern Sudan By Aleks Phillips Published 11 October 2026 At least 72 civilians who had been prospecting for gold in a border region of Sudan have been killed in air strikes, a regional rights group says. Emergency Lawyers, based in the Sudanese capital, Khartoum, said jets targeted the so-called artisanal miners at a popular gold mining site in Red Sea state on Saturday. Neither the Egyptian government nor the de facto Sudanese authorities have so far commented. Cairo has previously faced accusations of deadly strikes on gold prospectors as part of a crackdown on illicit activity along its southern border. Emergency Lawyers noted the previous alleged attacks and said they represented not only a violation of Sudan's sovereign territory but demonstrated the government's lack of control over the region. "The deliberate targeting of unarmed civilians violates international humanitarian law and the right to life," it said in a statement on Sunday. "These acts may constitute war crimes." It noted that its death toll was provisional and could rise.

stories.title: Questions remain over Ebola patient who travelled across three nations undetected
stories.summary: Image source, EPA Image caption, Nearly 70 potential contacts have been placed under quarantine in Nairobi By Wycliffe Muia Published 10 October 2026 A Kenyan businessman was able to spend time in one of the regions worst-affected by Ebola, then travel to two more countries before his illness was identified. The 40-year-old - who was only diagnosed with the deadly infectious disease after arriving seriously ill at a Nairobi hospital - became Kenya's first confirmed case. He died two days later on 5 October. That his infection went undetected at multiple health facilities in the Democratic Republic of Congo and two airport health screenings in Uganda and Kenya has raised serious questions about these nations' biosecurity during a significant outbreak. More than 4,000 people have died from Ebola in DR Congo this year, in what is the second most deadly known outbreak to date.

stories.title: In the Shadows review – true tale of Ramla Ali’s remarkable rise through the boxing ranks is a knockout
stories.summary: Fraught with danger … Jasmine Jobson in In the Shadows View image in fullscreen Fraught with danger … Jasmine Jobson in In the Shadows Review In the Shadows review – true tale of Ramla Ali’s remarkable rise through the boxing ranks is a knockout Jasmine Jobson goes the distance as the British-Somalian boxer battling pain from her past and her family’s disapproval in a heavyweight, tick-the-boxes production T he true-life success story of boxer Ramla Ali is confidently told in this capable picture from screenwriter Ursula Rani Sarma and documentary director Anthony Wonke, in his feature-film debut. Ali is the British-Somali boxer who escaped to the UK from the Somali civil war with her family as a refugee, and in 2021 became the first person to box for Somalia at Olympic Games . The boxing significance of her last name is actually not mentioned in the film – and I never noticed it until it flashed up in a kind of “fight card” intertitle before her first competitive bout. She is fiercely played by Jasmine Jobson, from TV’s Top Boy; her supportive white Muslim-convert husband Richard – a hugely important figure in enabling Ramla to break away from her disapproving family and do as she wants – is played by Finn Cole, and her abusive trainer Clinton is Gershwyn Eustache Jr. This is a film that takes you through the classic boxing-movie scenes fluently enough: the nervous first appearance in the gym, the overbearing quasi-parental coach, the heartstopping fight debut.

stories.title: ICJ judge Navi Pillay wins Nobel peace prize for promoting international law
stories.summary: 1:11 Nobel peace prize winner Navi Pillay jokes about sharing award with Donald Trump – video ICJ judge Navi Pillay wins Nobel peace prize for promoting international law Committee recognises work of South African who chaired UN commission that concluded Israel was guilty of genocide in Gaza The Nobel peace prize has been awarded to Navi Pillay, the South African former UN human rights chief who chaired the UN commission that concluded Israel was guilty of genocide in Gaza . The Norwegian Nobel committee said Pillay, who is serving as a judge at the international court of justice (ICJ), has “shown that legal measures can help prevent acts of war and violence”. “Navi Pillay’s commitment to universal legal principles and her firm moral compass are constants in a long career,” the committee said, mentioning her early work defending Nelson Mandela under South Africa’s apartheid regime, serving on the international criminal tribunal, and then as the UN high commissioner for human rights, as well as chairing the UN independent international commission of inquiry on the occupied Palestinian territory. That commission concluded last year that the state of Israel was guilty of genocidal acts in Gaza “with the specific intent to destroy Palestinians in Gaza”, and said the country’s prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, its president, Isaac Herzog, and its former defence minister Yoav Gallant had “incited the commission of genocide”. “It is clear that there is an intent to destroy the Palestinians in Gaza through acts that meet the criteria set forth in the genocide convention,” Pillay said on the publication of the commission’s findings in September last year. Israel refused to cooperate with the commission, arguing it was biased, and rejected its report as “scandalous”. The Israeli foreign ministry reacted furiously to news of Pillay’s award on Friday. “If there were an award for lies, hatred, and blood libels, Navi Pillay wouldn’t just be a contender.

stories.title: Why Zimbabwe tycoon 'Sir Wicknell' was loved and hated in Africa
stories.summary: Image source, Zanu-PF Image caption, Wicknell Chivayo, who had a fleet of personalised luxury cars, loved white Rolls-Royces By Ish Mafundikwa Reporting from Harare Published 8 October 2026 Wicknell Chivayo, the Zimbabwean tycoon who died in a helicopter crash along with his wife Lucy Muteke last week, divided opinion in life and continues to do so in death. He called himself "Sir Wicknell", a nod to the embellishment that epitomised his lifestyle - and a nickname some used for the 45-year-old who packed enough controversy into his short life to last several lifetimes. He was relentlessly self-documenting, building much of his public persona on social media, where he posed with piles of cash and announced the cars and money he gave to people whom he considered deserving. Chivayo delighted in displaying his access to heads of state across Africa and showing off his possessions, conducting video tours of his fleet of expensive cars, mainly Rolls-Royces, with vanity plates, watches and a vast collection of designer shoes. His admirers saw a fabulously wealthy man sharing his good fortune.
